age.evidence: Adult male C57/BL6 mice (3-months old) were used in this study

sex.evidence: Adult male C57/BL6 mice (3-months old) were used in this study

dosing.evidence: mice were i.p. injected as mentioned above with DMT (2 mg/kg) alone or in combination with ritanserin (0.2 µg/animal) during 21 consecutive days. All intraperitoneal treatments were administered 1 h after clorgyline (1 mg/kg, ip) injection.

day_night_flipped.evidence: Mice housed in a 12-h light-dark cycle animal facility

assays.assay_description: Spatial learning and memory test with a learning curve (~5 days), probe trial, and 3 days of cued learning. Measures included escape latency, platform crosses, and time in target annulus.

application_type.evidence: DMT (2 mg/kg) alone or in combination with ritanserin (0.2 µg/animal) during 21 consecutive days

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were freely swimming in the pool

food_restriction.evidence: Morris water maze pool — food not accessible during recording

water_restriction.evidence: animal is in water during testing

time_to_assay.evidence: DMT was intraperitoneally injected on alternating days for 21 days. Then, behavioral tests were performed for 10 days

sample_size.evidence: Twelve animals per experimental group were used.

outcomes.summary: DMT-treated mice showed reduced escape latency on days 4-5 of the learning curve and in the probe trial, and performed more platform crosses and spent more time in the target annulus compared to controls. Cued learning was unchanged, ruling out motor/motivational confounds.
outcomes.statistics: two-way mixed ANOVA; * P < 0.05; ** P < 0.01; *** P < 0.001 versus the control group; # P < 0.05 versus DMT + ritanserin group
outcomes.evidence: During the learning curve, there were significant differences between groups only on days 4 and 5... In the probe trial, DMT and DMT + ritanserin groups showed a significant reduction in escape latency compared with the control group.

B1_num_measures.evidence: escape latency, platform crosses, time in target annulus, cued learning latency

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: across-day learning curve is between-session, not within-session temporal dynamics

B4_ethological.evidence: escape latency and zone time only

B6_cognitive.evidence: Morris water maze test of spatial learning and memory

D1_continuity.evidence: learning curve, probe trial, and 3 days of cued learning

D3_recording_days.evidence: learning curve days 1-5, probe trial, 3 days cued learning

D5_followup.evidence: behavioral tests performed after 21-day dosing regimen, with animals sacrificed on day 31

assays.assay_description: Episodic memory test measuring exploration time, number of approaches, and latency to first approach for a novel vs. familiar object.

application_type.evidence: DMT (2 mg/kg) alone or in combination with ritanserin (0.2 µg/animal) during 21 consecutive days

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were freely moving in the arena

food_restriction.evidence: standard NOR apparatus — food not accessible during recording

water_restriction.evidence: standard NOR apparatus — water not accessible during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: DMT was intraperitoneally injected on alternating days for 21 days. Then, behavioral tests were performed for 10 days

sample_size.evidence: Twelve animals per experimental group were used.

outcomes.summary: DMT-treated mice spent more time exploring the novel object, made more approaches to it, and showed a shorter latency to first approach compared with controls, indicating improved episodic memory. DMT + ritanserin animals also showed enhanced novel-object exploration.
outcomes.statistics: * P < 0.05 versus the control group; # P < 0.05; ## P < 0.01; ### P < 0.001 versus old object
outcomes.evidence: the DMT group showed a longer exploration time of the new object and a greater number of approaches to it... differences in the latency of the first approach and exploration time between DMT and control groups.

B1_num_measures.evidence: exploration time, number of approaches, latency to first approach

B4_ethological.evidence: exploration time of objects, not natural behaviours scored separately

B6_cognitive.evidence: novel object recognition tests episodic memory

E5_enrichment.evidence: objects are test stimuli, not enrichment

D1_continuity.evidence: familiarization and test sessions typical for NOR within 10-day behavioral block

D3_recording_days.evidence: NOR typically has familiarization and test days within the 10-day behavioral block

D5_followup.evidence: behavioral testing began after 21-day dosing regimen

judge_notes: Only behavioural assays in the paper are Morris Water Maze and Novel Object Recognition; all other experiments are in vitro neurosphere assays or in vivo immunohistochemistry (BrdU/nestin/DCX/NeuN counts) and were excluded as non-behavioural per rubric.
Sex n_male reconciled: only male mice used; for behavioural studies, 12 per group × 3 groups (control, DMT, DMT+ritanserin) = 36 total males.
Dosing schedule: 21 days of alternating-day i.p. injections classified as 'chronic' (>7 days, ~11 doses), overriding 'repeated' label from some candidates.
DOI taken from the paper text (Supplementary Information line: 10.1038/s41398-020-01011-0).
B1 for MWM scored 2 (4-6 measures: learning-curve escape latency, probe escape latency, platform crosses, time in target annulus, cued-learning latency).
B2 scored 0: across-day learning curve is between-session, not within-session temporal dynamics per rubric.
D5 scored Yes for both assays because behavioural testing took place over days 22-31, ≥24 h after the last DMT dose during the 21-day dosing window.
